system.description:
Demi-Orcs — Perorch / Piryrch

Les Demi-Orcs, appelés Perorch au singulier et Piryrch au pluriel, sont issus du mélange des Hommes et des Orcs. Ils sont parfois confondus avec les Uruk-hai, mais constituent une Race distincte : moins uniformément massive, plus humaine d’apparence et beaucoup plus apte à se mêler aux populations humaines.

Ils servent comme agents, espions, officiers, gardes spéciaux, assassins et intermédiaires entre sociétés humaines et armées de l’Ombre. Leur apparition organisée est surtout associée à Saruman au Troisième Âge.

Une origine volontairement obscure

La manière exacte dont ils furent engendrés n’est pas clairement expliquée. Ils peuvent descendre de captifs, de lignées humaines progressivement corrompues, d’expériences délibérées de Saruman ou de communautés frontalières déjà mêlées. Cette incertitude doit être conservée.

Différence avec les Uruk-hai

Les grands Uruks sont conçus comme soldats immédiatement reconnaissables ; les Demi-Orcs excellent dans l’infiltration, l’espionnage et la manipulation. Ils peuvent commander des Orcs communs ou traiter avec des alliés humains sans révéler immédiatement leur nature.

Les agents de Saruman

Saruman les emploie pour infiltrer des communautés, observer des seigneurs, recruter des mercenaires, surveiller les Dunlendings, transmettre des ordres, organiser sabotages et assassinats ou diriger des éclaireurs. Ceux possédant du sang dunlending peuvent adopter vêtements, accent et coutumes locales.

Apparence et diversité

Ils ont une carrure comparable à celle des Uruk-hai mais des traits plus humains. Les hommes mesurent environ 1,73 m et les femmes 1,65 m. Leur peau peut être grise, mate, brunâtre ou maladivement pâle, leurs cheveux noirs ou gris et leurs yeux noirs ou brun rougeâtre.

Certains passent presque pour des Hommes ; d’autres révèlent leur ascendance par une mâchoire lourde, des dents épaisses, un nez aplati, des oreilles légèrement pointues, une voix rauque ou une odeur corporelle forte.

Longévité et endurance

Ils peuvent vivre entre 250 et 500 ans, bien que peu atteignent cet âge en raison des guerres, missions et rivalités. Ils voyagent longtemps sans dormir, supportent les marches forcées et bénéficient d’une résistance notable à la chaleur et au froid.

Vision et lumière

Ils voient extrêmement bien dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée dans les ténèbres absolues. Contrairement aux Orcs communs, ils ne sont pas réellement affaiblis par le Soleil, même s’ils préfèrent les lieux sombres et couverts.

Identité et milieu

Leur mode de vie dépend du groupe humain ou orc qui les a élevés : garnison, communauté dunlendinge, Isengard, bande de mercenaires, brigands ou famille humaine dissimulant leur origine. La Race porte leurs aptitudes physiques ; la Culture doit refléter leur éducation.

Une existence entre Hommes et Orcs

Parmi les Orcs, ils sont jugés trop humains, privilégiés ou dangereux. Parmi les Hommes, ils risquent le rejet, l’exécution ou l’exploitation. Cette double exclusion nourrit souvent ambition, ressentiment et désir de pouvoir.

Société et hiérarchie

Ils respectent la puissance, la terreur et l’efficacité. Leur statut dépend de leur capacité à servir un maître, inspirer la peur et obtenir des résultats. Ils deviennent lieutenants, contremaîtres, espions, gardes du corps, chefs de bande, interrogateurs ou assassins.

Famille

Les habitudes matrimoniales dépendent entièrement du groupe auquel ils appartiennent. Dans un environnement orc, les unions sont contrôlées par la force ; dans une communauté humaine, elles peuvent imiter les coutumes locales sous une fausse identité. Les descendants présentent des degrés variables d’ascendance orc.

Tempérament et ambition

Ils sont généralement cruels, jaloux, ambitieux, égoïstes et soupçonneux. Ils valorisent pouvoir, secret, utilité, force, tromperie et réussite personnelle. Leur intelligence sociale et leur résistance au Soleil leur donnent souvent le sentiment d’être supérieurs aux Orcs communs.

Méfiance et dissimulation

Ils apprennent à multiplier les identités, conserver des moyens de fuite, accumuler des secrets et observer les faiblesses de leurs supérieurs. Le jeu d’acteur, le déguisement et la maîtrise des accents sont essentiels à leur survie.

Religion

La majorité révère les Ténèbres et la puissance. Ils peuvent servir Sauron, Saruman, le Roi-Sorcier ou une autre puissance obscure. Leur dévotion repose plus souvent sur la peur et l’ambition que sur une foi sincère. Un infiltré peut simuler les rites d’une communauté humaine.

Langues

Le westron, l’orquien et le Parler Noir sont leurs langues principales. Le dunael est courant chez les lignées liées aux Dunlendings. Les agents expérimentés apprennent plusieurs dialectes humains et orcs.

Relations

Les Orcs communs les craignent et les jalousent. Les Uruk-hai sont des alliés et rivaux plus puissants physiquement. Ils haïssent particulièrement les Elfes et les Dúnedain. Leurs relations avec les Dunlendings sont centrales dans les plans de Saruman.

Vêtements, armures et armes

Leur habillement dépend de leur couverture. Les tenues dunael comprennent tunique de peau, braies de cuir, veste à carreaux ternes, torc d’acier et cheveux en petites tresses. Toutes les armures leur sont accessibles.

Ils utilisent épées, arcs, dagues, haches, masses, cimeterres, lances, marteaux, fouets, armes à griffes et flèches barbelées.

Manière de combattre

Ils combinent brutalité orc et meilleure discipline humaine. Ils privilégient embuscades, attaques nocturnes, assassinat, armes dissimulées, infiltration préalable, neutralisation des officiers et fuite organisée.

Compétences, magie et professions

Leur formation peut couvrir jeu d’acteur, embuscade, dressage, manœuvres en armure, corruption, spéléologie, escalade, désamorçage de pièges, commandement, travail du cuir et du métal, équitation, filature, tactique, pistage et tromperie.

Toutes les professions sont accessibles sauf le Barbare et les voies réservées à d’autres peuples. Ils sont adaptés aux rôles de Combattant, Roublard, Voleur, Rôdeur, espion, assassin, garde du corps, sorcier ou guérisseur orc.

Origine et sélection

La manière exacte dont les Demi-Orcs furent engendrés n’est pas clairement expliquée. Plusieurs interprétations sont possibles : descendants de captifs humains, lignées progressivement corrompues, créations délibérées de Saruman, communautés frontalières mêlées ou résultat de pratiques plus anciennes reprises par Isengard. Cette incertitude doit être conservée plutôt que remplacée par une vérité unique.

Diversité des lignées

Les Demi-Orcs ne possèdent pas une apparence uniforme. Leur physionomie dépend largement de l’ascendance humaine utilisée. Une lignée dunlendinge peut présenter cheveux noirs, teint sombre ou rougeaud, carrure robuste et accent dunael ; d’autres lignées peuvent refléter des Hommes de l’Est ou du Sud. Cette diversité facilite leur infiltration et permet plusieurs origines culturelles sans modifier la Race elle-même.

Jeu d’acteur et déguisement

L’aptitude à imiter les Hommes est essentielle aux agents destinés à l’infiltration. Ils apprennent à modifier leur accent, dissimuler leurs dents, contrôler leur posture, imiter des coutumes, porter des vêtements locaux, inventer une histoire crédible et feindre peur, loyauté ou amitié. Un individu habile peut passer pour un mercenaire, un garde, un Dunlending, un voyageur ou un brigand humain.

Relations avec les Dunlendings

Les Demi-Orcs de Saruman sont particulièrement liés aux Dunlendings. Certains possèdent directement du sang dunael et peuvent se fondre dans leurs communautés. Saruman peut les utiliser pour attiser la haine du Rohan, surveiller les chefs, détourner des ressources, recruter des guerriers, éliminer des opposants ou transmettre de faux messages. Les Dunlendings découvrant leur vraie nature peuvent y voir une abomination ou la preuve de la duplicité d’Isengard.

Half-orcs — Perorch / Piryrch

Half-orcs, called Perorch in the singular and Piryrch in the plural, are born from the mingling of Men and Orcs. They are sometimes confused with the Uruk-hai, but constitute a distinct Race: less uniformly massive, more human in appearance and far better able to blend into human populations.

They serve as agents, spies, officers, special guards, assassins and intermediaries between human societies and the armies of the Shadow. Their organised appearance is especially associated with Saruman during the Third Age.

A deliberately obscure origin

The exact manner in which they were bred is not clearly explained. They may descend from captives, from human lineages gradually corrupted, from deliberate experiments by Saruman, or from frontier communities already of mixed blood. This uncertainty should be preserved.

Difference from the Uruk-hai

The great Uruks are designed as immediately recognisable soldiers; Half-orcs excel at infiltration, espionage and manipulation. They can command Common Orcs or deal with human allies without immediately revealing their nature.

Saruman's agents

Saruman uses them to infiltrate communities, observe lords, recruit mercenaries, watch the Dunlendings, carry orders, organise sabotage and assassinations, or command scouts. Those with Dunlending blood can adopt local clothing, accent and customs.

Appearance and diversity

They have a build comparable to that of the Uruk-hai but more human features. Men stand around 1.73 m and women around 1.65 m. Their skin may be grey, swarthy, brownish or sickly pale, their hair black or grey, and their eyes black or reddish-brown.

Some can almost pass for Men; others reveal their ancestry through a heavy jaw, thick teeth, flattened nose, slightly pointed ears, harsh voice or strong body odour.

Longevity and endurance

They may live between 250 and 500 years, although few reach such an age because of wars, missions and rivalries. They can travel for long periods without sleep, endure forced marches and possess notable resistance to both heat and cold.

Vision and light

They see extremely well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. Unlike Common Orcs, they are not truly weakened by sunlight, even though they prefer dark and covered places.

Identity and upbringing

Their way of life depends on the human or Orcish group that raised them: a garrison, a Dunlending community, Isengard, a mercenary company, brigands or a human family concealing their origin. The Race carries their physical abilities; Culture should reflect their upbringing.

A life between Men and Orcs

Among Orcs they are judged too human, privileged or dangerous. Among Men they risk rejection, execution or exploitation. This double exclusion often feeds ambition, resentment and a desire for power.

Society and hierarchy

They respect power, terror and efficiency. Their status depends on their ability to serve a master, inspire fear and produce results. They become lieutenants, overseers, spies, bodyguards, gang leaders, interrogators or assassins.

Family

Marriage customs depend entirely on the group to which they belong. In an Orcish environment, unions are controlled by force; in a human community, they may imitate local customs under a false identity. Their descendants display varying degrees of Orcish ancestry.

Temperament and ambition

They are generally cruel, jealous, ambitious, selfish and suspicious. They value power, secrecy, usefulness, strength, deception and personal success. Their social intelligence and resistance to sunlight often give them a sense of superiority over Common Orcs.

Distrust and concealment

They learn to maintain multiple identities, keep means of escape, accumulate secrets and observe the weaknesses of their superiors. Acting, disguise and mastery of accents are essential to their survival.

Religion

Most revere Darkness and power. They may serve Sauron, Saruman, the Witch-king or another dark power. Their devotion rests more often on fear and ambition than on sincere faith. An infiltrator may imitate the rites of a human community.

Languages

Westron, Orcish and the Black Speech are their principal languages. Dunael is common among lineages connected to the Dunlendings. Experienced agents learn several human and Orcish dialects.

Relations

Common Orcs fear and envy them. Uruk-hai are more physically powerful allies and rivals. They particularly hate Elves and the Dúnedain. Their relations with the Dunlendings are central to Saruman's plans.

Clothing, armour and weapons

Their clothing depends on their cover identity. Dunael dress may include a hide tunic, leather breeches, a dull chequered jacket, a steel torc and hair worn in small braids. All forms of armour are available to them.

They use swords, bows, daggers, axes, maces, scimitars, spears, hammers, whips, clawed weapons and barbed arrows.

Fighting style

They combine Orcish brutality with better human discipline. They favour ambushes, night attacks, assassination, concealed weapons, prior infiltration, elimination of officers and organised retreat.

Skills, magic and professions

Their training may include acting, ambush, animal training, manoeuvring in armour, bribery, caving, climbing, trap disarming, leadership, leatherwork and metalwork, riding, shadowing, tactics, tracking and deception.

All professions are available except Barbarian and paths reserved for other peoples. They are well suited to roles such as Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Ranger, spy, assassin, bodyguard, sorcerer or Orcish healer.

Origin and selection

The exact manner in which Half-orcs were bred is not clearly explained. Several interpretations are possible: descendants of human captives, lineages gradually corrupted, deliberate creations of Saruman, mixed frontier communities, or the result of older practices later adopted by Isengard. This uncertainty should be preserved rather than replaced with a single definitive truth.

Diversity of bloodlines

Half-orcs do not possess a uniform appearance. Their features depend greatly on the human ancestry involved. A Dunlending line may show black hair, a dark or ruddy complexion, a powerful build and a Dunael accent; other lineages may reflect Men of the East or South. This diversity facilitates infiltration and allows several cultural origins without changing the Race itself.

Acting and disguise

The ability to imitate Men is essential to agents intended for infiltration. They learn to alter their accent, hide their teeth, control their posture, imitate customs, wear local clothing, invent a credible history and feign fear, loyalty or friendship. A skilled individual can pass for a mercenary, guard, Dunlending, traveller or human brigand.

Relations with the Dunlendings

Saruman's Half-orcs are especially closely tied to the Dunlendings. Some directly possess Dunael blood and can blend into their communities. Saruman may use them to inflame hatred of Rohan, watch chiefs, divert resources, recruit warriors, eliminate opponents or carry false messages. Dunlendings who discover their true nature may see them as an abomination or as proof of Isengard's treachery.

Place in character creation

The Half-orcs — Perorch / Piryrch Race is available in the Third and Fourth Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the character's human origin, the group in which they were raised, any connection with Saruman, their cover identity, the break with their master and the reason why an adventuring group tolerates their presence.

Les habitudes matrimoniales dépendent entièrement du groupe auquel ils appartiennent. Half-orcs — Perorch / Piryrch

They serve as agents, spies, officers, special guards, assassins and intermediaries between human societies and the armies of the Shadow. Their organised appearance is especially associated with Saruman during the Third Age.

A deliberately obscure origin

The exact manner in which they were bred is not clearly explained. They may descend from captives, from human lineages gradually corrupted, from deliberate experiments by Saruman, or from frontier communities already of mixed blood. This uncertainty should be preserved.

Difference from the Uruk-hai

The great Uruks are designed as immediately recognisable soldiers; Half-orcs excel at infiltration, espionage and manipulation. They can command Common Orcs or deal with human allies without immediately revealing their nature.

Saruman's agents

Saruman uses them to infiltrate communities, observe lords, recruit mercenaries, watch the Dunlendings, carry orders, organise sabotage and assassinations, or command scouts. Those with Dunlending blood can adopt local clothing, accent and customs.

Appearance and diversity

Some can almost pass for Men; others reveal their ancestry through a heavy jaw, thick teeth, flattened nose, slightly pointed ears, harsh voice or strong body odour.

Longevity and endurance

They may live between 250 and 500 years, although few reach such an age because of wars, missions and rivalries. They can travel for long periods without sleep, endure forced marches and possess notable resistance to both heat and cold.

Vision and light

They see extremely well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. Unlike Common Orcs, they are not truly weakened by sunlight, even though they prefer dark and covered places.

Identity and upbringing

Their way of life depends on the human or Orcish group that raised them: a garrison, a Dunlending community, Isengard, a mercenary company, brigands or a human family concealing their origin. The Race carries their physical abilities; Culture should reflect their upbringing.

A life between Men and Orcs

Among Orcs they are judged too human, privileged or dangerous. Among Men they risk rejection, execution or exploitation. This double exclusion often feeds ambition, resentment and a desire for power.

Society and hierarchy

They respect power, terror and efficiency. Their status depends on their ability to serve a master, inspire fear and produce results. They become lieutenants, overseers, spies, bodyguards, gang leaders, interrogators or assassins.

Family

Marriage customs depend entirely on the group to which they belong. In an Orcish environment, unions are controlled by force; in a human community, they may imitate local customs under a false identity. Their descendants display varying degrees of Orcish ancestry.

Temperament and ambition

They are generally cruel, jealous, ambitious, selfish and suspicious. They value power, secrecy, usefulness, strength, deception and personal success. Their social intelligence and resistance to sunlight often give them a sense of superiority over Common Orcs.

Distrust and concealment

They learn to maintain multiple identities, keep means of escape, accumulate secrets and observe the weaknesses of their superiors. Acting, disguise and mastery of accents are essential to their survival.

Religion

Most revere Darkness and power. They may serve Sauron, Saruman, the Witch-king or another dark power. Their devotion rests more often on fear and ambition than on sincere faith. An infiltrator may imitate the rites of a human community.

Westron, Orcish and the Black Speech are their principal languages. Dunael is common among lineages connected to the Dunlendings. Experienced agents learn several human and Orcish dialects.

Common Orcs fear and envy them. Uruk-hai are more physically powerful allies and rivals. They particularly hate Elves and the Dúnedain. Their relations with the Dunlendings are central to Saruman's plans.

They use swords, bows, daggers, axes, maces, scimitars, spears, hammers, whips, clawed weapons and barbed arrows.

Fighting style

They combine Orcish brutality with better human discipline. They favour ambushes, night attacks, assassination, concealed weapons, prior infiltration, elimination of officers and organised retreat.

Skills, magic and professions

Their training may include acting, ambush, animal training, manoeuvring in armour, bribery, caving, climbing, trap disarming, leadership, leatherwork and metalwork, riding, shadowing, tactics, tracking and deception.

All professions are available except Barbarian and paths reserved for other peoples. They are well suited to roles such as Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Ranger, spy, assassin, bodyguard, sorcerer or Orcish healer.

Origin and selection

The exact manner in which Half-orcs were bred is not clearly explained. Several interpretations are possible: descendants of human captives, lineages gradually corrupted, deliberate creations of Saruman, mixed frontier communities, or the result of older practices later adopted by Isengard. This uncertainty should be preserved rather than replaced with a single definitive truth.

Diversity of bloodlines

Half-orcs do not possess a uniform appearance. Their features depend greatly on the human ancestry involved. A Dunlending line may show black hair, a dark or ruddy complexion, a powerful build and a Dunael accent; other lineages may reflect Men of the East or South. This diversity facilitates infiltration and allows several cultural origins without changing the Race itself.

Acting and disguise

The ability to imitate Men is essential to agents intended for infiltration. They learn to alter their accent, hide their teeth, control their posture, imitate customs, wear local clothing, invent a credible history and feign fear, loyalty or friendship. A skilled individual can pass for a mercenary, guard, Dunlending, traveller or human brigand.

Relations with the Dunlendings

Saruman's Half-orcs are especially closely tied to the Dunlendings. Some directly possess Dunael blood and can blend into their communities. Saruman may use them to inflame hatred of Rohan, watch chiefs, divert resources, recruit warriors, eliminate opponents or carry false messages. Dunlendings who discover their true nature may see them as an abomination or as proof of Isengard's treachery.

Place in character creation

The Half-orcs — Perorch / Piryrch Race is available in the Third and Fourth Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the character's human origin, the group in which they were raised, any connection with Saruman, their cover identity, the break with their master and the reason why an adventuring group tolerates their presence.

They combine Orcish brutality with better human discipline. They favour ambushes, night attacks, assassination, concealed weapons, prior infiltration, elimination of officers and organised retreat.

Their training may include acting, ambush, animal training, manoeuvring in armour, bribery, caving, climbing, trap disarming, leadership, leatherwork and metalwork, riding, shadowing, tactics, tracking and deception.

All professions are available except Barbarian and paths reserved for other peoples. They are well suited to roles such as Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Ranger, spy, assassin, bodyguard, sorcerer or Orcish healer.

A Dunlending line may show black hair, a dark or ruddy complexion, a powerful build and a Dunael accent; other lineages may reflect Men of the East or South. This diversity facilitates infiltration and allows several cultural origins without changing the Race itself.

Acting and disguise

The ability to imitate Men is essential to agents intended for infiltration. They learn to alter their accent, hide their teeth, control their posture, imitate customs, wear local clothing, invent a credible history and feign fear, loyalty or friendship. A skilled individual can pass for a mercenary, guard, Dunlending, traveller or human brigand.

Saruman's Half-orcs are especially closely tied to the Dunlendings. Some directly possess Dunael blood and can blend into their communities. Saruman may use them to inflame hatred of Rohan, watch chiefs, divert resources, recruit warriors, eliminate opponents or carry false messages. Dunlendings who discover their true nature may see them as an abomination or as proof of Isengard's treachery.

Place in character creation

The Half-orcs — Perorch / Piryrch Race is available in the Third and Fourth Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the character's human origin, the group in which they were raised, any connection with Saruman, their cover identity, the break with their master and the reason why an adventuring group tolerates their presence.

Ils peuvent vivre entre 250 et 500 ans, bien que peu atteignent cet âge en raison des guerres, missions et rivalités. Ils voyagent longtemps sans dormir, supportent les marches forcées et bénéficient d’une résistance notable à la chaleur et au froid.

Vision et lumière

Ils voient extrêmement bien dans la pénombre et conservent une perception limitée dans les ténèbres absolues. Contrairement aux Orcs communs, ils ne sont pas réellement affaiblis par le Soleil, même s’ils préfèrent les lieux sombres et couverts.

Identité et milieu

Leur mode de vie dépend du groupe humain ou orc qui les a élevés : garnison, communauté dunlendinge, Isengard, bande de mercenaires, brigands ou famille humaine dissimulant leur origine. La Race porte leurs aptitudes physiques ; la Culture doit refléter leur éducation.

Une existence entre Hommes et Orcs

Parmi les Orcs, ils sont jugés trop humains, privilégiés ou dangereux. Parmi les Hommes, ils risquent le rejet, l’exécution ou l’exploitation. Cette double exclusion nourrit souvent ambition, ressentiment et désir de pouvoir.

Société et hiérarchie

Ils respectent la puissance, la terreur et l’efficacité. Leur statut dépend de leur capacité à servir un maître, inspirer la peur et obtenir des résultats. Ils deviennent lieutenants, contremaîtres, espions, gardes du corps, chefs de bande, interrogateurs ou assassins.

Famille

Les habitudes matrimoniales dépendent entièrement du groupe auquel ils appartiennent. Dans un environnement orc, les unions sont contrôlées par la force ; dans une communauté humaine, elles peuvent imiter les coutumes locales sous une fausse identité. Les descendants présentent des degrés variables d’ascendance orc.

Tempérament et ambition

Ils sont généralement cruels, jaloux, ambitieux, égoïstes et soupçonneux. Ils valorisent pouvoir, secret, utilité, force, tromperie et réussite personnelle. Leur intelligence sociale et leur résistance au Soleil leur donnent souvent le sentiment d’être supérieurs aux Orcs communs.

Méfiance et dissimulation

Ils apprennent à multiplier les identités, conserver des moyens de fuite, accumuler des secrets et observer les faiblesses de leurs supérieurs. Le jeu d’acteur, le déguisement et la maîtrise des accents sont essentiels à leur survie.

Religion

La majorité révère les Ténèbres et la puissance. Ils peuvent servir Sauron, Saruman, le Roi-Sorcier ou une autre puissance obscure. Leur dévotion repose plus souvent sur la peur et l’ambition que sur une foi sincère. Un infiltré peut simuler les rites d’une communauté humaine.

Langues

Le westron, l’orquien et le Parler Noir sont leurs langues principales. Le dunael est courant chez les lignées liées aux Dunlendings. Les agents expérimentés apprennent plusieurs dialectes humains et orcs.

Relations

Les Orcs communs les craignent et les jalousent. Les Uruk-hai sont des alliés et rivaux plus puissants physiquement. Ils haïssent particulièrement les Elfes et les Dúnedain. Leurs relations avec les Dunlendings sont centrales dans les plans de Saruman.

Vêtements, armures et armes

Leur habillement dépend de leur couverture. Les tenues dunael comprennent tunique de peau, braies de cuir, veste à carreaux ternes, torc d’acier et cheveux en petites tresses. Toutes les armures leur sont accessibles.

Ils utilisent épées, arcs, dagues, haches, masses, cimeterres, lances, marteaux, fouets, armes à griffes et flèches barbelées.

Manière de combattre

Ils combinent brutalité orc et meilleure discipline humaine. Ils privilégient embuscades, attaques nocturnes, assassinat, armes dissimulées, infiltration préalable, neutralisation des officiers et fuite organisée.

Compétences, magie et professions

Leur formation peut couvrir jeu d’acteur, embuscade, dressage, manœuvres en armure, corruption, spéléologie, escalade, désamorçage de pièges, commandement, travail du cuir et du métal, équitation, filature, tactique, pistage et tromperie.

Toutes les professions sont accessibles sauf le Barbare et les voies réservées à d’autres peuples. Ils sont adaptés aux rôles de Combattant, Roublard, Voleur, Rôdeur, espion, assassin, garde du corps, sorcier ou guérisseur orc.

Origine et sélection

La manière exacte dont les Demi-Orcs furent engendrés n’est pas clairement expliquée. Plusieurs interprétations sont possibles : descendants de captifs humains, lignées progressivement corrompues, créations délibérées de Saruman, communautés frontalières mêlées ou résultat de pratiques plus anciennes reprises par Isengard. Cette incertitude doit être conservée plutôt que remplacée par une vérité unique.

Diversité des lignées

Les Demi-Orcs ne possèdent pas une apparence uniforme. Leur physionomie dépend largement de l’ascendance humaine utilisée. Une lignée dunlendinge peut présenter cheveux noirs, teint sombre ou rougeaud, carrure robuste et accent dunael ; d’autres lignées peuvent refléter des Hommes de l’Est ou du Sud. Cette diversité facilite leur infiltration et permet plusieurs origines culturelles sans modifier la Race elle-même.

Jeu d’acteur et déguisement

L’aptitude à imiter les Hommes est essentielle aux agents destinés à l’infiltration. Ils apprennent à modifier leur accent, dissimuler leurs dents, contrôler leur posture, imiter des coutumes, porter des vêtements locaux, inventer une histoire crédible et feindre peur, loyauté ou amitié. Un individu habile peut passer pour un mercenaire, un garde, un Dunlending, un voyageur ou un brigand humain.

Relations avec les Dunlendings

Les Demi-Orcs de Saruman sont particulièrement liés aux Dunlendings. Certains possèdent directement du sang dunael et peuvent se fondre dans leurs communautés. Saruman peut les utiliser pour attiser la haine du Rohan, surveiller les chefs, détourner des ressources, recruter des guerriers, éliminer des opposants ou transmettre de faux messages. Les Dunlendings découvrant leur vraie nature peuvent y voir une abomination ou la preuve de la duplicité d’Isengard.

Place dans la création de personnage

La Race Demi-Orcs — Perorch / Piryrch est disponible aux Troisième et Quatrième Âges et doit rester Restreinte. Le joueur doit préciser l’origine humaine, le groupe d’éducation, le lien éventuel avec Saruman, l’identité de couverture, la rupture avec le maître et la raison pour laquelle un groupe d’aventuriers le tolère.

Half-orcs — Perorch / Piryrch

Half-orcs, called Perorch in the singular and Piryrch in the plural, are born from the mingling of Men and Orcs. They are sometimes confused with the Uruk-hai, but constitute a distinct Race: less uniformly massive, more human in appearance and far better able to blend into human populations.

They serve as agents, spies, officers, special guards, assassins and intermediaries between human societies and the armies of the Shadow. Their organised appearance is especially associated with Saruman during the Third Age.

A deliberately obscure origin

The exact manner in which they were bred is not clearly explained. They may descend from captives, from human lineages gradually corrupted, from deliberate experiments by Saruman, or from frontier communities already of mixed blood. This uncertainty should be preserved.

Difference from the Uruk-hai

The great Uruks are designed as immediately recognisable soldiers; Half-orcs excel at infiltration, espionage and manipulation. They can command Common Orcs or deal with human allies without immediately revealing their nature.

Saruman's agents

Saruman uses them to infiltrate communities, observe lords, recruit mercenaries, watch the Dunlendings, carry orders, organise sabotage and assassinations, or command scouts. Those with Dunlending blood can adopt local clothing, accent and customs.

Appearance and diversity

They have a build comparable to that of the Uruk-hai but more human features. Men stand around 1.73 m and women around 1.65 m. Their skin may be grey, swarthy, brownish or sickly pale, their hair black or grey, and their eyes black or reddish-brown.

Some can almost pass for Men; others reveal their ancestry through a heavy jaw, thick teeth, flattened nose, slightly pointed ears, harsh voice or strong body odour.

Longevity and endurance

They may live between 250 and 500 years, although few reach such an age because of wars, missions and rivalries. They can travel for long periods without sleep, endure forced marches and possess notable resistance to both heat and cold.

Vision and light

They see extremely well in dim light and retain limited perception in absolute darkness. Unlike Common Orcs, they are not truly weakened by sunlight, even though they prefer dark and covered places.

Identity and upbringing

Their way of life depends on the human or Orcish group that raised them: a garrison, a Dunlending community, Isengard, a mercenary company, brigands or a human family concealing their origin. The Race carries their physical abilities; Culture should reflect their upbringing.

A life between Men and Orcs

Among Orcs they are judged too human, privileged or dangerous. Among Men they risk rejection, execution or exploitation. This double exclusion often feeds ambition, resentment and a desire for power.

Society and hierarchy

They respect power, terror and efficiency. Their status depends on their ability to serve a master, inspire fear and produce results. They become lieutenants, overseers, spies, bodyguards, gang leaders, interrogators or assassins.

Family

Marriage customs depend entirely on the group to which they belong. In an Orcish environment, unions are controlled by force; in a human community, they may imitate local customs under a false identity. Their descendants display varying degrees of Orcish ancestry.

Temperament and ambition

They are generally cruel, jealous, ambitious, selfish and suspicious. They value power, secrecy, usefulness, strength, deception and personal success. Their social intelligence and resistance to sunlight often give them a sense of superiority over Common Orcs.

Distrust and concealment

They learn to maintain multiple identities, keep means of escape, accumulate secrets and observe the weaknesses of their superiors. Acting, disguise and mastery of accents are essential to their survival.

Religion

Most revere Darkness and power. They may serve Sauron, Saruman, the Witch-king or another dark power. Their devotion rests more often on fear and ambition than on sincere faith. An infiltrator may imitate the rites of a human community.

Languages

Westron, Orcish and the Black Speech are their principal languages. Dunael is common among lineages connected to the Dunlendings. Experienced agents learn several human and Orcish dialects.

Relations

Common Orcs fear and envy them. Uruk-hai are more physically powerful allies and rivals. They particularly hate Elves and the Dúnedain. Their relations with the Dunlendings are central to Saruman's plans.

Clothing, armour and weapons

Their clothing depends on their cover identity. Dunael dress may include a hide tunic, leather breeches, a dull chequered jacket, a steel torc and hair worn in small braids. All forms of armour are available to them.

They use swords, bows, daggers, axes, maces, scimitars, spears, hammers, whips, clawed weapons and barbed arrows.

Fighting style

They combine Orcish brutality with better human discipline. They favour ambushes, night attacks, assassination, concealed weapons, prior infiltration, elimination of officers and organised retreat.

Skills, magic and professions

Their training may include acting, ambush, animal training, manoeuvring in armour, bribery, caving, climbing, trap disarming, leadership, leatherwork and metalwork, riding, shadowing, tactics, tracking and deception.

All professions are available except Barbarian and paths reserved for other peoples. They are well suited to roles such as Fighter, Rogue, Thief, Ranger, spy, assassin, bodyguard, sorcerer or Orcish healer.

Origin and selection

The exact manner in which Half-orcs were bred is not clearly explained. Several interpretations are possible: descendants of human captives, lineages gradually corrupted, deliberate creations of Saruman, mixed frontier communities, or the result of older practices later adopted by Isengard. This uncertainty should be preserved rather than replaced with a single definitive truth.

Diversity of bloodlines

Half-orcs do not possess a uniform appearance. Their features depend greatly on the human ancestry involved. A Dunlending line may show black hair, a dark or ruddy complexion, a powerful build and a Dunael accent; other lineages may reflect Men of the East or South. This diversity facilitates infiltration and allows several cultural origins without changing the Race itself.

Acting and disguise

The ability to imitate Men is essential to agents intended for infiltration. They learn to alter their accent, hide their teeth, control their posture, imitate customs, wear local clothing, invent a credible history and feign fear, loyalty or friendship. A skilled individual can pass for a mercenary, guard, Dunlending, traveller or human brigand.

Relations with the Dunlendings

Saruman's Half-orcs are especially closely tied to the Dunlendings. Some directly possess Dunael blood and can blend into their communities. Saruman may use them to inflame hatred of Rohan, watch chiefs, divert resources, recruit warriors, eliminate opponents or carry false messages. Dunlendings who discover their true nature may see them as an abomination or as proof of Isengard's treachery.

Place in character creation

The Half-orcs — Perorch / Piryrch Race is available in the Third and Fourth Ages and should remain Restricted. The player should specify the character's human origin, the group in which they were raised, any connection with Saruman, their cover identity, the break with their master and the reason why an adventuring group tolerates their presence.
